item.text: I’ll trace the MIME detection and image support code, record a checkpoint, then update the implementation and run the relevant existing tests. I’ll keep the investigation to repository code and tests.

# Checkpoint

Task: Resolve HEIC/JXL Safari 17+ image support and simplify MIME detection.

Plan:
1. Inspect repository guidance and the MIME/browser/version utilities plus relevant tests.
2. Implement the requested MIME mapping and Safari/macOS/iOS capability checks.
3. Run relevant existing tests and summarize the changes.
EOF

item.text: I found two checked-in copies of Drive’s upload MIME parser: the app source and its `drive-store` package mirror. I’ll keep both in sync. MIME resolution will use a meaningful `File.type` first, fall back to the filename extension when the browser reports no type or `application/octet-stream`, and avoid file reads. The image allowlist will gate HEIC-family and JXL types on Safari 17+ for macOS/iOS.

The implementation is in place: Safari’s `Mobile Safari` UA is handled alongside desktop Safari, and the HEIC check covers the existing HEIC/HEIF MIME variants. I’m reviewing the diff and will run the shared preview tests plus Drive’s existing image/upload tests.

item.text:
Implemented HEIC/JXL image support and MIME detection updates.

- Added `image/jxl` to [constants.ts](/app/packages/shared/lib/drive/constants.ts) and mapped `.jxl` to that MIME type.
- Added Safari 17+ checks for macOS and iOS in [mimetype.ts](/app/packages/shared/lib/helpers/mimetype.ts), and gated HEIC/HEIF variants and JXL in supported image detection.
- Simplified MIME detection in both Drive parser copies to prefer a useful `File.type`, then use the filename extension when the type is missing or generic.

**Verification:** Drive thumbnail scaling and media info tests passed. The shared browser suite could not start because its Playwright Chromium binary is missing. Shared and Drive Store type checks reported errors in unrelated crypto, documents, and Drive config code.
